The concerned member state can submit its observations within one month from the date on which the Commission communicates the evaluation.

The Commission evaluates the observations referred to in paragraph 4 as soon as possible. It lifts the suspension when the concerned Member State demonstrates that it has taken necessary measures to ensure the satisfactory fulfillment of the conditions set out in this regulation.
The portion of loans granted to the three member states that are the largest beneficiaries does not exceed 60% of the maximum amount specified in Article 6.
The loan agreement must include the necessary provisions concerning controls and audits required by Article 223, paragraph 4 of the financial regulation.
The Commission presents to the European Parliament and the Council an annual report on the use of financial assistance.
If necessary, the report is accompanied by a proposal for an extension of the period of availability of the SAFE instrument.
Joint ventures are eligible for support under the SAFE instrument only if they meet the eligibility criteria set forth in this Article.

The joint procurement and acquisition procedures for defense products include the participation requirements outlined in paragraphs 3 to 13 and 15 of this article, without prejudice to the terms set forth in Article 17.

The contracting parties and subcontractors participating in the joint acquisition are established within the Union, in an EULEM member state of the EEE or in Ukraine, and have their executive management structures there. They are not subject to control by a third country that is neither an EULEM member state of the EEE nor Ukraine, or by an entity from another third country that is not established within the Union, in an EULEM member state of the EEE or in Ukraine.

In derogation of paragraph 3, in order to take into account industrial cooperation with partners from third countries, joint acquisitions involving a subcontractor whose share of market value is between 15% and 35%, which is not established within the Union, in an EAEU member state of the EEE or in Ukraine, without having its executive management structures there, shall be eligible for support under the SAFE instrument provided that at least one of the following conditions is met:
A direct contractual relationship linked to the defense product has been established between the contractor and the sub-contractor before the effective date of this regulation.

The contractor undertakes to study within two years whether it is possible to replace the goods supplied by the said subcontractor with another free from any original Union restriction, and to comply with technical requirements and deadlines.

In derogation from paragraph 3, an entity established in the Union and controlled by a third country or by an entity of another third country may participate in a joint acquisition if it has undergone filtering as defined in Regulation (EU) 2019/452, and where necessary, appropriate mitigation measures have been taken, or if it provides verified guarantees by the Member State in which is established the contracting party or subcontractor participating in the joint acquisition. The guarantees provide assurance that the contracting party or subcontractor’s participation in the joint acquisition does not run counter to the interests of the Union and its Member States in matters of security and defense as they are defined within the framework of the Common Foreign and Security Policy under Title V of the Treaty on the European Union.

The guarantees referred to in paragraph 5 can be based on a standardized model provided by the Commission and form part of the specifications, ensuring uniform use across the Union. The guarantees specifically attest that measures are in place for joint acquisitions to ensure:

- That all necessary conditions have been met,
- That the relevant documents have been properly prepared,
- That the technical aspects have been adequately addressed,
- That the financial arrangements are fully compliant with EU regulations.

b) The control exercised over the contracting or subcontracting party participating in the joint acquisition is not exercised in a manner that limits or restricts its ability to execute the order and produce results.

A third country or an entity of a third country cannot have access to classified information related to joint acquisition and that employees or other persons participating in the joint acquisition possess a national security clearance issued by an EU member state in accordance with national legislative and regulatory provisions.

The adjudicating party that acquires a joint venture submits to the Commission a notification concerning the measures of mitigation applied in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2019/452 or the guarantees referred to in paragraph 5. Additional information on the measures of mitigation applied or the guarantees is made available to the Commission upon request.

The infrastructure, installation, property and resources of contractors and subcontractors participating in an integrated acquisition that are used for the purpose of such an acquisition must be located within the territory of a member state, a member state of the ALEE member of EEE or Ukraine. If the contractors or subcontractors participating in the integrated acquisition do not have readily available substitutes or infrastructure, installations, property and resources on the territory of a member state, a member state of the ALEE member of EEE or Ukraine, they may use their infrastructure, installations, property and resources situated or held outside these territories so long as this use does not contravene the interests of the Union and its member states in matters of security and defense.

The contracting and subcontracting parties participating in the joint acquisition can be considered to meet the eligibility criteria set out in paragraphs 3 to 7 when they have fulfilled equivalent conditions as those specified under Regulation (EU) 2018/1092 (9), Regulation (EU) 2021/697 (10), Regulation (EU) 2023/1525 or Regulation (EU) 2023/2418 of the European Parliament and Council, provided that no further modifications do not undermine their compliance with these conditions.

The cost of components originating outside the Union, from member states of the AELE EEE, and Ukraine is not higher than 35% of the estimated cost of the final product's components. For joint acquisitions benefiting from the SAFETY instrument, no component comes from any third country that goes against the interests of the Union and its member states in terms of security and defense.

For defense products falling under the second category as specified in Article 1, paragraph 2, item b), contractors have the capacity to decide without any restrictions imposed by third-party countries or entities of third-party countries on the definition, adaptation, and evolution of the design of acquired defense products, including legal power to replace or remove components subject to such restrictions imposed by third-party countries or entities of third-party countries.

For the purposes of this Article, "subcontractor participating in an integrated acquisition" shall mean any legal entity that provides critical inputs, possessing unique essential attributes for the operation of a product, which is allocated at least 15% of market value, and which requires access to classified information for market execution.

Member States ensure that acquisition procedures and related markets for other defense-related products resulting from joint acquisitions benefiting from the support of the SAFE instrument contain appropriate eligibility criteria to protect the Union's and its Member States' interests in matters of security and defence.

Members specify in the plan referred to in Article 7 the eligibility criteria as set out in paragraphs 3 to 11 and 13 to 15 of this present article without prejudice to any conditions established in the agreements referred to in Article 17. Financial assistance is conditional on the presentation, at the same time as the request for payment, of the information indicated in the operational arrangements referred to in Article 10.

Member states may use the financial assistance provided under the SAFE instrument to finance their participation in acquisition procedures conducted in accordance with Article 168, paragraph 2 or 3, of the regulatory framework. In this case, derogating from Articles 168, paragraphs 2 and 3, of the regulatory framework, third countries participating in joint acquisitions can also participate in all market passing mechanisms envisaged in Article 168, paragraphs 2 and 3, of the regulatory framework and benefit therefrom.

The Union can conclude bilateral or multilateral agreements with countries on the path to accession, potential candidate states, and other candidates except Ukraine, as well as with third countries with which the Union has concluded a security and defense partnership (non-binding instrument) in order to open these countries and their territories to eligibility criteria set out in Article 16, in accordance with paragraphs 2 and 3 of this article.

The bilateral or multilateral agreement mentioned in paragraph 1 specifies how the eligibility criteria referred to in Article 16 should be applied. It specifically sets out:

- The manner in which the eligibility conditions specified in Article 16 shall apply.
- In particular:

The conditions and terms related to the participation of contractors and subcontractors from third countries in a joint acquisition under the SAFE instrument, including conditions regarding the location of management execution structures and control exercised by third countries or entities thereof.

The rules concerning the location of infrastructure, facilities, property, and resources used in joint acquisitions for defense products or other defense-related products produced under joint acquisition instruments within the scope of SAFE market tenders.

d) rules concerning the cost of imported components, including at least 10% of components originating from the European Union, a member country of the ALEE, or Ukraine and up to 50% of components not originating in the European Union, any ALEE member country, Ukraine, or a third party party to the agreement.

e) rules concerning restrictions imposed by non-parties to the agreement or entities established on their territory regarding the definition, adaptation, and evolution of the defense acquisition product's concept supported by the SAFE instrument.
The bilateral or multilateral agreement.
b) ensure fair balance in terms of contributions and benefits for third countries.
b) fixes the conditions under which the third country must provide financial contributions to the Union;
c) establishes any other appropriate measure regarding the security of acquired product supply.
d) contributes to an increased standardization of defense systems and to greater interoperability between the capabilities of member states and these other third-party countries.

The contributions mentioned in paragraph 3, point b) are external revenue sources as per Article 21, paragraph 5 of the financial regulation and are used to support defense industries within the Union, Ukraine's Ukrainian defense industry, and Ukraine according to these programs' rules.

When an acquisition is supported under the terms of the SAFE instrument, paragraphs 2 to 4 apply to a framework agreement or existing contract that involves the purchase of defense products and is financed at least in whole or in part by one of the participating member states through the loan granted under the SAFE instrument, without providing substantial modification possibilities. When applying paragraphs 2 and 3, the awarding authority that concluded the framework agreement or the contract obtains prior approval from the company with which it has concluded said framework agreement or contract.

A member state's adjudicating authority may modify an existing defense-related agreement or contract when such an agreement or contract was concluded with an entity meeting criteria equivalent to those outlined in Articles 16, paragraphs 3-13, of this regulation, for the addition of new participating countries' adjudicating authorities as parties to that agreement or contract. Article 29, paragraph 2, first sentence, of Directive 2009/81/EC does not apply to adjudicating authorities that were not initially parties to the agreement or contract.

Under Article 29, paragraph 2, third subparagraph of Directive 2009/81/EC, an adjudicator from one Member State may make substantial amendments to quantities fixed in a framework agreement or a tender whose estimated value exceeds the thresholds set out in Article 8 of Directive 2009/81/EC, provided that such a framework agreement or this tender was concluded with an entity meeting criteria equivalent to those stated in Articles 16, paragraphs 3 to 13, of this Regulation, and where this amendment is strictly necessary for the application of the second subparagraph of this article.
For the purpose of calculating the value as specified in paragraph 3, the updated value serves as the reference point when the market includes an indexing clause.

A notification of such an adjudicator's modification of a framework agreement or a tender in the cases referred to in paragraph 2 or 3 of this Article shall be published in the Official Journal of the European Union in accordance with Article 32 of Directive 2009/81/EC.

In cases covered by paragraphs 2 and 3, the principle of equal rights and obligations applies between adjudicating powers that are parties to the framework agreement or tender, particularly concerning the cost of additional quantities acquired.

Acquisitions involving at least one member state benefiting from financial assistance under the SAFE instrument are deemed to satisfy the urgency condition resulting from crisis situations for the purposes of Article 28, paragraph 1, point c) of Directive 2009/81/EC.

Under the present regulation, supplies, acquisitions intra-community and imports of defense-related or other products intended for defense purposes that are carried out in the context of acquisition markets benefiting from the support under the instrument SAFE are exempted from value-added tax (VAT) as provided for in Directive 2006/112/EC. The exemption is subject to deduction of VAT paid at an earlier stage.

The VAT exemption certificate listed in Annex serves to confirm that the operation meets the requirements for enjoying VAT exemption provided for under this regulation. This certificate is stamped with the seals of competent authorities of the member state acquiring defense products or other products intended for defense purposes within the framework of procurement resulting from acquisitions benefiting from the support of the SAFE instrument and must be kept by the supplier of these products in their registers.

The Commission uses a secure exchange system to facilitate the exchange of classified information and sensitive data between the Commission and its Member States, as well as, if necessary, with contractors or other final recipients.

The Commission has access to information, including classified, strictly necessary for verifying payment terms and conducting verifications, examinations, audits, investigations, reports, as well as controls and audits referred to in Article 14.

The Commission and Member States may carry out communication activities to ensure the visibility of Union assistance in the context of investment plans for European defense industry, including through joint communications with concerned national authorities while taking security requirements into account. In case it is necessary, the Commission can ensure that support under the SAFE instrument is communicated and recognized through a funding statement.

Member states benefiting from financial assistance under the SAFE instrument ensure the visibility of Union assistance while duly taking into account security requirements, including displaying the EU emblem and an appropriate funding declaration mentioning "with the support of the European Union - SAFE," particularly when promoting joint acquisitions and their results, providing targeted, coherent, effective, and proportional information to various audiences, notably media and the general public.

The Commission implements information and communication actions related to the SAFE instrument, the measures taken under it, and the results achieved. In case of need, the Commission informs its European Parliament representation offices, and associates them with these actions.
This regulation shall come into force on the day following its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union.
